prompt: Before the store, why did ticking a session on the course page leave the week's total unchanged?

choices.text: The checkbox's `change` event never reached `CoursePage`
choices.why: It did: the course page's copy changed.

choices.text: Each component had its own resource and its own copy
choices.why: Right. The tick changed only `CoursePage`'s.

choices.text: `Week` is OnPush, and OnPush ignores clicks elsewhere
choices.why: A signal both read would have updated it; there was none.

choices.text: The dev server cached the first answer to `courses.json`
choices.why: Both requests were answered; each copy was its own.

prompt: Before the store, how many requests for `/courses.json` did one load of the page make?
What makes `PlannerStore` a service, as far as Angular is concerned?

choices.text: It extends Angular's `Service` base class, as the CLI writes it
choices.why: There is no such class; it extends nothing.

choices.text: Its name ends with `Store`
choices.why: The name is for people; Angular reads none of it.

choices.text: Nothing special: an injectable class with no template
choices.why: Right. Everything in it is lesson 10.

choices.text: It was created by `ng generate service`
choices.why: The CLI only wrote a file; a class written by hand is the same.

prompt: Why does the store write `this.data.hasValue() ? this.data.value().courses : []` rather than `this.data.value()?.courses ?? []`?

choices.text: `?.` does not work inside a `computed`
choices.why: It works anywhere a TypeScript expression does.

choices.text: `value()` throws in the error state
choices.why: Right. The check comes first, so the computed never throws.

choices.text: `hasValue()` starts the request if it has not started
choices.why: It only reads the state; the resource started on its own.

choices.text: `hasValue()` is faster than reading the value
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: The CLI command that wrote `planner-store.ts` was `npx ng generate ___ planner-store`.
After both components injected the store, the tick showed 140 minutes done. What carried the change to `Week`?

choices.text: `CoursePage` emitted an output that `Week` listened to
choices.why: Neither knows the other exists.

choices.text: The store reloaded `courses.json` after the toggle
choices.why: There was one request, before the tick.

choices.text: Change detection ran over the whole page because of the click
choices.why: The page is zoneless and OnPush; a click alone redraws nothing.

choices.text: `Week`'s `totals` read the store's `sessions` signal, which changed
choices.why: Right. One signal, read by both.

prompt: The components declare `protected readonly store = inject(PlannerStore)`. Why `protected` and not `private`?

choices.text: The templates read `store`
choices.why: Right. A template reaches `protected` members, not `private` ones.

choices.text: `private` fields cannot hold an injected value
choices.why: They can; `PlannerStore` keeps its resource in one.

choices.text: `protected` lets subclasses replace the store
choices.why: Nothing here subclasses a component.

choices.text: `private` would give each component its own store
choices.why: Visibility has nothing to do with which injector answers.

prompt: `this.store.sessions.set([])` stopped the build. What did the error say?

choices.text: `NG0201`: no provider for `Session[]`
choices.why: It was a TypeScript error at build time, not an injection error.

choices.text: `TS2339`: `set` does not exist on `Signal<Session[]>`
choices.why: Right. A computed is a read-only signal.

choices.text: `TS2341`: `sessions` is private
choices.why: That error was about `data`; `sessions` is public.

choices.text: Nothing: it compiled, and cleared the list on the page
choices.why: The compiler refused both lines.

prompt: Which of these keep a component from changing the store's data behind its back? Choose every one that does.

choices.text: The resource is `private`
choices.why: Right. Only the store's own methods reach it.

choices.text: `courses` and `sessions` are `computed`, with no `set`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The store is `providedIn: 'root'`
choices.why: That decides who shares it, not who may write to it.

choices.text: The components are OnPush
choices.why: Change detection does not guard data.

choices.text: Changes go through a named method, `toggle`
choices.why: Right. The one place that changes a session.

prompt: For state in a plain writable signal, `this.state.___()` hands out a signal that reads it and cannot write it.
Why did the week's totals move into the store while the rows stayed in `Week`?

choices.text: The rows need a template of their own, and a service has none
choices.why: The rows are a `computed`, which a service can hold.

choices.text: One holds for any screen; the other suits one
choices.why: Right. Facts move, a screen's choices stay.

choices.text: The totals were slow to compute in a component
choices.why: Speed did not come into it.

choices.text: A store may not hold more than four computed values
choices.why: There is no such limit.

prompt: After the move, `Week` no longer injects `TODAY`, yet the week test that provides `TODAY` still passed. Why?

choices.text: The test was skipped because it no longer matched
choices.why: Five tests ran and passed.

choices.text: `Week` still reads `new Date()` as a fallback
choices.why: `Week` reads no date at all now.

choices.text: The store asked the test's injector, and the test's `useValue` answered
choices.why: Right. Whoever asks, the injector answers.

choices.text: The test checks only that `Week` can be created
choices.why: It checks the range of the week of 28 October.

prompt: `minutesThisWeek(courseId)` is a method, not a `computed`. Does a `computed` that calls it update when a session changes?

choices.text: No, only signals are ever tracked by a `computed`, never methods
choices.why: What is tracked is the read of `sessions()` inside the method.

choices.text: Yes: `sessions()` is read while the `computed` runs
choices.why: Right. Tracking follows the reads, wherever they are written.

choices.text: Only if the method is marked `@Injectable`
choices.why: That decorator is for classes, and tracking does not need it.

choices.text: Only once, the first time it is called
choices.why: It updates every time a session it read changes.

prompt: `CoursePage` was given `providers: [PlannerStore]`. What did the tick show?

choices.text: An `NG0201`, as two providers clash
choices.why: A component provider over a root one is normal, and silent.

choices.text: 140 done, as before
choices.why: The week kept its own store's copy.

choices.text: Two requests, and 90 done: a second store with a second copy
choices.why: Right. `CoursePage`'s question stopped at its own injector.

choices.text: A build error, since `PlannerStore` is already `providedIn: 'root'`
choices.why: Nothing failed to compile.

prompt: Match each kind of state with where to provide its service.

pairs.left: shared by every screen of the application
separate for each instance of one component
one area's, loaded with a group of routes

right_distractors: the `imports` of the component that uses it

prompt: Where is a per-component service the right choice?

choices.text: For the planner's sessions, so each screen is independent
choices.why: Independent copies are this lesson's defect.

choices.text: For the half-filled fields of a form shown several times on a page
choices.why: Right. Each copy is meant to be separate and to go with its form.

choices.text: For anything that is loaded from a server
choices.why: Where data comes from does not decide who shares it.

choices.text: Whenever the service is used by one component today
choices.why: Today's single user says nothing about the state's scope.

prompt: How can you tell, reading the code, whether a service is really shared?

choices.text: By the word `Store` or `Service` in its name
choices.why: Names say nothing about where it is provided.

choices.text: By `@Injectable()` on the class
choices.why: That only lets Angular build it.

choices.text: By whether its methods change signals
choices.why: That is about state, not scope.

choices.text: By `providedIn` and every `providers:` list that names it
choices.why: Right. Whoever writes the provider decides the scope.

prompt: A new screen needs the number of sessions still to do this week. Where should it be computed?

choices.text: In `PlannerStore`, as a computed of its own
choices.why: Right. It is a fact about the planner, the same for any screen.

choices.text: In the new screen's component, with its own `resource`
choices.why: That would be a third copy of the data.

choices.text: In `Week`, which already counts the week
choices.why: `Week` no longer counts it; the store does.

choices.text: In `planner.ts`, read by the template directly
choices.why: A template can only read what its component exposes.
